eyebrow: TEARDOWN · A FIELD GUIDE TO STRUCTURED EXPLANATIONS
title: Make the idea visible.
lede: A good visual explanation does more than look organized. It helps the reader see a boundary, follow a behavior, or make a decision. Here is a small language for doing that well.

blocks.title: The agent explains. The renderer composes.
blocks.body_md: Give the agent a vocabulary of ideas, not a blank HTML canvas. **JSON carries the argument; the renderer carries the visual system.** The result stays editable, inspectable, and consistent.

cells.label: Compose explanations
cells.detail: Fifteen block types, selected for the idea rather than the decoration.

cells.label: Open without a server
cells.detail: One HTML file, with embedded styling and no runtime requests.

cells.label: Verify source claims
cells.detail: A renderer can check structure. The author still owns the evidence.

cells.label: Understand any Markdown
cells.detail: A small, safe grammar. Use dedicated blocks for richer structures.

blocks.title: Separate meaning from presentation
blocks.summary: One stable boundary makes the rest of the workflow simpler.

blocks.body_md: A useful explanation has two jobs: make a claim clear, then make it credible. Those jobs should survive a change in colors or typography. Here, the document is the durable source; HTML is a generated reading surface.

blocks.title: Two ways to make a visual explanation

columns.label: Free-form HTML
columns.body_md:
A flexible canvas for a bespoke illustration.

- Every document carries layout decisions.
- Content and styling can become tangled.
- Review includes executable markup.

columns.label: Structured blocks
columns.body_md:
A shared visual language for recurring explanatory work.

- The author chooses the form of the idea.
- The renderer owns consistent presentation.
- Validation catches structural mistakes early.

blocks.title: A small pipeline with a clear trust boundary

nodes.label: Question + source material
nodes.detail: The reader’s actual uncertainty, plus inspected evidence.

nodes.label: Structured explanation
nodes.detail: The agent selects blocks and writes the source JSON.

nodes.label: Schema + relationship checks
nodes.detail: Shape, block types, node references, and row widths.

nodes.label: Standalone HTML
nodes.detail: Escaped content, embedded CSS, no browser scripts.

edges.label: Render only when all checks pass

blocks.caption: This is the actual package boundary. Source investigation happens before rendering, not inside it.

blocks.text_md: The renderer imports the bundled schema validator before generating HTML. Its output embeds CSS and contains no browser script. Those are implementation properties, not claims about the source material being explained.

blocks.title: Pick the form that reveals the idea
blocks.summary: A flow, a sequence, and a state machine answer different questions.

blocks.title: Three views, three questions
blocks.caption: Choose by the reader’s uncertainty, not by which diagram looks more sophisticated.

blocks.title: From source file to reading surface
blocks.caption: Success path only. Invalid input produces an error instead of an output file.

blocks.title: A document’s authoring lifecycle

states.label: Draft
states.detail: The content is still being shaped.

states.label: Structurally valid
states.detail: The JSON meets the schema and relationship rules.

states.label: Ready to share
states.detail: The author has also checked claims and visual clarity.

transitions.label: Evidence and rendered document have been inspected

blocks.caption: An illustrative authoring model, not persistent state maintained by the CLI. Valid JSON is not proof of a sound explanation.

blocks.title: “Unsupported” is a conclusion, not a default.
blocks.body_md: If you have not checked whether a capability exists, label it **unknown**. A confident-looking card should not turn missing evidence into a negative finding.

blocks.title: Keep the artifact easy to inspect
blocks.summary: A small package boundary, a plain command, and a source file you can edit.

entries.responsibility: CLI input and safe file output

blocks.title: Render, then open the result
blocks.caption: Run from the package root after creating output/. Existing output is protected unless --force is supplied.

items.context: The closed block union in schema version 1.0.

items.label: Reading artifact
items.context: No accompanying assets needed after rendering.

blocks.title: Finish with understanding, not just valid JSON
blocks.summary: Structure can be checked automatically. The argument still needs judgment.

items.label: Validate the document
items.detail: This showcase was rendered through the same validation boundary as other documents.

items.label: Inspect the claims and their sources
items.detail: For a real teardown, inspect the actual system; examples are not evidence about it.

items.label: Check the narrow-screen view
items.detail: Keep important labels readable and split overloaded diagrams.

items.label: Mark unresolved facts honestly
items.detail: Illustrative status: a missing source should remain an explicit question.

terms.definition: The allowed structure of a document: its fields, values, and block shapes.
The program that turns a valid content document into a reading surface.
An observation or source that supports a particular claim. A polished layout is not evidence.
